name: tag-group
title: Tag group
summary: Lays out a set of tags or chips in lines that wrap, spaced for what it holds, and exposes the set as one named list; the members stay what they are, and after a chip is removed focus goes on to the next.

anatomy.description: The set: lines of members that start at the start edge and wrap. It draws nothing of its own — no container, no fill, no edge, no padding and no label — and is exposed as one list.
A tag or a chip of the set: placed and spaced by the group, exposed as an item of its list, and otherwise drawn and behaving as it does anywhere.

props.name: spacing
props.description: What the set holds, which decides the distances between its members. tags: static tags, as close as words of one group. chips: chips, which take input, with lines far enough apart that each chip keeps its whole touch target.

props.name: label
props.description: The accessible name of the set ("Tags", "Filters", "Suggested fonts"). It is not drawn: a set that needs a visible name stands under the product's own heading or text, and still takes this. Optional where the set is plain from what surrounds it, recommended for a set of chips.

props.name: selection
props.description: Whether the group holds the selection of its filter chips. none: it holds none, and each filter chip holds its own selected, as alone. single: at most one filter chip is on at a time, named by value. multiple: any number are on, named by values. While it is single or multiple the set is one Tab stop and the arrow keys move between its chips.

props.name: value
props.description: The value of the filter chip that is on while selection is single; null puts none on. The group sets it when a person switches a chip and emits change; the product may also set it.

props.name: values
props.description: The values of the filter chips that are on while selection is multiple: a list of strings (the platforms take a set). An empty list puts none on.

events.name: change
events.description: While selection is single or multiple, a person switched a filter chip of the set: carries value (single) or values (multiple) after the change, which the group now holds. In place of the chip's own change, which stops at the group (TGR-19).

items.name: tag
items.summary: A Tag of the set: the tag component, placed and spaced by the group and exposed as an item of its list, otherwise drawn and read as it is anywhere.

props.name: label
props.description: Its text, as the Tag's label.

props.name: variant
props.description: Its look, as the Tag's variant.

props.name: status
props.description: What it reports, as the Tag's status.

props.name: size
props.description: Its height, as the Tag's size. Give every member of a group the same size.

props.name: icon
props.description: The glyph in the Tag's icon slot, by its name in the system's icon set. Empty for none. It is how a fixture fills that slot; in an application the slot is filled as the Tag's own spec says.

items.name: chip
items.summary: A Chip of the set: the chip component, placed and spaced by the group and exposed as an item of its list, otherwise drawn and behaving as it does anywhere, with its own state, events and Tab stop.

props.name: kind
props.description: What it does, as the Chip's kind.

props.name: label
props.description: Its text and accessible name, as the Chip's label.

props.name: size
props.description: Its height, as the Chip's size. Give every member of a group the same size.

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether a filter chip is on, as the Chip's selected. While selection is none the chip holds it; while selection is single or multiple the group sets it from value or values (TGR-17).

props.name: value
props.description: What the group's value and values name a filter chip by, as the Chip's value. Unique within the set; needed while selection is single or multiple.

props.name: disabled
props.description: As the Chip's disabled: one chip of a set may be disabled by itself.

props.name: href
props.description: The destination of an action chip, as the Chip's href: it makes the chip a link.

props.name: removeLabel
props.description: The accessible name of an input chip's remove action, as the Chip's removeLabel.

props.name: icon
props.description: The glyph in the Chip's icon slot, by its name in the system's icon set. Empty for none. It is how a fixture fills that slot; in an application the slot is filled as the Chip's own spec says.

events.name: click
events.description: The chip was activated, as the Chip's click.

events.name: change
events.description: A filter chip was switched, as the Chip's change. While selection is single or multiple it stops at the group, whose own change carries the selection (TGR-19).

events.name: remove
events.description: The person asked to remove an input chip, as the Chip's remove. The product removes it; the group then places the rest and moves focus (TGR-9).

behavior.text: THE tag group SHALL lay out its members in lines: from its start edge, in the order they were given, comp.tag-group.gap.tags apart along a line WHILE spacing is tags and comp.tag-group.gap.chips apart WHILE spacing is chips, each member at its own size and centred on the middle of its line. It SHALL be as wide as its layout gives it and as tall as its lines, SHALL draw no container, fill, edge or elevation of its own, SHALL add no padding around its members, and SHALL NOT draw its label.
behavior.verify: Under the default system three medium tags stand 8 apart on one line 24 high; three medium chips stand 8 apart on one line 32 high.

behavior.text: WHEN a member does not fit in what is left of a line THE tag group SHALL put it, whole, at the start of a new line below, comp.tag-group.row-gap.tags below the line above WHILE spacing is tags and comp.tag-group.row-gap.chips WHILE spacing is chips, measured between the visible bounds of the tallest members of the two lines; it SHALL NOT cut, shrink or split a member to keep it on a line, SHALL NOT scroll its lines, and SHALL NOT hide a member or stand a count in its place: every member it is given is shown. WHERE one member alone is wider than the group THE tag group SHALL give it the group's width on a line of its own, and the member SHALL then cut its own label as its own spec says (TAG-5, CHP-17).
behavior.verify: Under the default system two lines of medium tags are 8 apart and two lines of medium chips 16. Fixtures tags-wrap and chips-filters-wrap hold more members than any stage is wide. Unit: in a group 120 wide a tag with a long label is 120 wide, on its own line, with an ellipsis.

behavior.text: THE tag group SHALL keep its members in the order they were given: it SHALL NOT sort them, move a selected chip forward or group them by kind, and the order in which focus moves through its chips and in which assistive technology reads its members SHALL be that order — along each line from its start, and line after line from the top.

THE tag group SHALL take from spacing only the distances of TGR-1 and TGR-2: spacing SHALL NOT change what a member is, how it is drawn or what the group exposes. WHERE the platform can tell what its members are, WHILE spacing is tags and a member takes input (a chip) THE tag group SHALL still render and in debug builds report that a set of chips wants spacing chips, because the lines of tags stand closer than a chip's touch target is high.

WHILE the hit areas that two neighbouring chips extend beyond their visible bounds (CHP-5, CHP-21) overlap THE tag group SHALL give every press on a chip's visible bounds to that chip, and a press in the gap between two chips — along a line or between two lines — to the nearer one, so that neighbouring hit areas meet at the middle of the gap. comp.tag-group.row-gap.chips is what keeps each chip's target whole between two lines: at sys.target.touch minus a chip's height or more, no hit areas overlap, as under the default system's value for a medium chip; a small chip on wrapped lines, and a layer that narrows the gap, have targets that meet between the lines.
behavior.verify: Under the default system two wrapped lines of medium chips give every chip 48 of height to a touch: 32 and half of 16 on each side.

behavior.text: THE tag group SHALL NOT restyle its members: each SHALL render from its own tokens at its own size, answer hover, focus and press itself, hold its own state (a filter chip its selected, which the group sets WHILE selection is single or multiple, TGR-17), emit its own events (but the change of a filter chip the group holds, TGR-19) and keep its own role and name inside the item the group exposes it as (TGR-7). WHILE selection is none each chip SHALL be its own Tab stop — an input chip one, the chip itself, whose remove action is not a stop and which Backspace or Delete removes (CHP-18, CHP-19, CHP-23) — in the order of TGR-3, and the tag group SHALL NOT handle arrow keys, Home or End, SHALL keep no selection of its own, SHALL NOT make its filter chips exclusive, and SHALL emit no event; what a selection changes is TGR-17 to TGR-21. The tag group itself SHALL NOT take focus, whatever its selection. The tag group has no size of its own: members of different sizes on one line are centred on it (TGR-1).

WHILE the tag group holds at least one member THE tag group SHALL expose itself to assistive technology as a list, named by label WHILE label is not empty, and each member as one item of that list, in the order of TGR-3, holding the member as the member exposes itself: a tag as its text (TAG-11), a chip as its button or its link with its state, an input chip with its remove action beside it. WHEN label changes THE tag group SHALL expose the new name at once. WHILE label is empty THE tag group SHALL still expose the list, unnamed. A platform that has no list role SHALL expose a container named by label that holds the members in order, and state that in its README.
behavior.verify: On the web: the accessibility tree has a list with the label as its name and one listitem per member; a filter chip inside its listitem is a button with its pressed state.

behavior.text: WHILE the tag group holds no member THE tag group SHALL draw nothing, take no space and expose nothing — no empty list and no name — and SHALL report nothing: a set that has no tags yet, or whose last filter was removed, is not a mistake. WHILE it holds one member THE tag group SHALL lay it out and expose it as a list of one.

WHEN a member leaves the tag group while focus is on it — on a chip or on its remove action — THE tag group SHALL move focus to the chip that follows it in the order of TGR-3, or to the chip before it WHERE none follows, on the chip itself and never on its remove action, so that a person who removes several entered items in a row goes on from where they were; it SHALL skip a member that takes no focus (a tag, a disabled chip). WHERE no member that takes focus is left THE tag group SHALL NOT move focus, having nowhere of its own to put it: the product moves it to the control that the set belongs to (CHP-22). THE tag group SHALL NOT remove a member itself and SHALL announce nothing.
behavior.verify: Unit: of five input chips, removing the focused third puts focus on the former fourth; removing the focused last puts it on the new last; pressing the remove action of a chip puts focus on the next chip, not on that chip's remove action.

behavior.text: WHEN a member is added, is removed or changes its size THE tag group SHALL place its members again by TGR-1 and TGR-2 and SHALL move every member whose place that changes from where it was drawn to its new place over comp.tag-group.motion.move-duration with comp.tag-group.motion.move-easing, along its line and from one line to another, without fading or scaling it; a change that comes while members move SHALL take each of them on from where it is drawn. A member that is added SHALL appear in its place at once and one that is removed SHALL leave at once. WHILE a line holds the same members in the same order as before the change, its members SHALL follow the change at once: a member that changes its size, at once or over a motion of its own, carries the members after it on its line, and a line whose height changes carries the lines below. THE tag group's own height SHALL follow its lines at once, and WHEN the width the layout gives the tag group changes THE tag group SHALL place its members again at once. WHERE motion is reduced THE tag group SHALL place its members again at once. A member that has focus while it moves SHALL keep it, its focus indicator moving with it, and THE tag group SHALL NOT move focus because a member was added.
behavior.verify: Web: of five filter chips on one line, removing the second moves the third to fifth toward the start over at least four frames, and the first does not move; a chip that grows until the last one goes to the next line moves that one there over at least four frames, and the ones before the chip do not move; a filter chip switched on in a line that keeps its members carries the chips after it a gap away in every frame, and the group starts no motion; with reduced motion, or when the group's width changes, every member is in its new place in the first frame.

behavior.text: WHILE the tag group holds content that is not a Tanrei tag or chip THE tag group SHALL still lay it out and expose it as a member, and in debug builds report it; a platform that cannot inspect its content SHALL state the rule in its README and docs page.

WHILE the text size is enlarged THE tag group SHALL keep its gaps and let its members grow as their own specs say (TAG-13, CHP-17), wrapping onto as many lines as they then need; at 200% no member SHALL be lost, lie over another or be cut by the group, and the group SHALL need scrolling in no direction of its own.

WHERE the platform draws with a person's own forced colors (the web's forced-colors mode, and a platform's equivalent where it has one) THE tag group SHALL draw nothing of its own there either: its members draw themselves as their own specs say (TAG-14), and the distances of TGR-1 and TGR-2 stay what tells them apart.

WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left THE tag group SHALL start every line at the right edge and place its members from right to left, in the order they were given, wrapping to a new line below as TGR-2 says; the order of focus and of reading SHALL stay the order of TGR-3. Each member's own content SHALL follow the layout direction as the member's spec says (TAG-15, CHP-25).
behavior.verify: Fixture chips-filters-rtl: the first chip is at the top right, and the second line starts at the right.

behavior.text: THE tag group SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the tag group is shown THE tag group SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping its members, their state and their focus.
behavior.verify: Test with the direction set on an ancestor inside the page or the view tree, not on the root, and again changed after the first render.

behavior.text: WHEN spacing names a value that the active design system does not have THE tag group SHALL render with the default value's tokens, and in debug builds report the unknown value.

WHILE selection is single or multiple THE tag group SHALL hold the selection of its filter chips by their value: it SHALL set each filter chip's selected to whether value equals the chip's value (single) or values holds it (multiple) WHEN selection, value or values changes, WHEN a filter chip arrives and WHEN a chip's value or kind changes, so that what each chip shows and exposes as its pressed state (CHP-11) is always the group's selection. A chip that is not a filter chip, a tag and other content take no part in it, and are laid out, reached and exposed as WHILE selection is none. WHEN value or values names no member THE tag group SHALL put nothing on for that name and report nothing, because a filter whose chip was taken away is not a mistake; WHEN a member leaves THE tag group SHALL leave value and values as they are and emit nothing. WHEN selection becomes none THE tag group SHALL leave each chip's selected as it then is and hold it no longer. WHEN selection names a value it does not have THE tag group SHALL behave as WHILE it is none, and in debug builds report the value.
behavior.verify: Unit: under selection multiple with values [open, review] the chips Open and Needs review are pressed and the others not; setting values to [blocked] makes Blocked the only pressed chip and emits nothing; a filter chip added with the value blocked arrives pressed.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is single or multiple, WHERE a filter chip's value is empty THE tag group SHALL leave that chip out of its selection — it keeps its own selected and its own change, as WHILE selection is none — and WHERE two filter chips share a value THE tag group SHALL put them on and off together, because they name one thing; in debug builds it SHALL report each, and it SHALL render either way.

WHEN the person switches a filter chip that has a value — by pointer, touch, Enter, Space or assistive technology — WHILE selection is single THE tag group SHALL set value to the chip's value WHERE the chip is now on, and switch every other filter chip off, or to null WHERE it is now off, because each chip is a toggle that says it is pressed and a pressed toggle that cannot be released would be untrue; WHILE selection is multiple THE tag group SHALL add the chip's value to values WHERE the chip is now on, or take it out WHERE it is now off. THE tag group SHALL then emit change exactly once, carrying value (single) or values (multiple), which it already holds, and SHALL stop the chip's own change at the group, so that a listener on the group or above it hears one change that carries the selection. THE tag group SHALL emit nothing WHEN the product sets selection, value or values.
behavior.verify: Unit: under single, pressing Oldest while Recently updated is on leaves only Oldest on and emits one change with value oldest; pressing Oldest again emits one change with value null. Under multiple, Space on Assigned to me emits one change with values that hold it. No change from a chip reaches a listener on the group.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is single or multiple and the group holds a chip that takes focus THE tag group SHALL be one stop in the focus order, in place of the stops TGR-6 gives each chip: the chip that last had focus WHILE it is still in the group and takes focus, otherwise the first filter chip that is on, otherwise the first chip that takes focus; every other chip, and with it its remove action, SHALL be out of the Tab order and stay focusable by the keys of this rule, by pointer and touch, and by assistive technology. WHILE a chip of the group has focus THE tag group SHALL move focus, without switching or removing anything: on Right Arrow to the chip drawn after it and on Left Arrow to the one drawn before it — in a right-to-left layout the same two keys the other way, so that an arrow always moves the way it points — on Home to the first chip and on End to the last, passing every member that takes no focus (a tag, a disabled chip); focus SHALL NOT wrap, and Up Arrow and Down Arrow SHALL do nothing: the members are one row in their order, however many lines draw it. Enter and Space SHALL stay the focused chip's own — Space switches a filter chip (CHP-11) — and so SHALL Backspace and Delete on an input chip (CHP-19).
behavior.verify: Unit: Tab reaches one chip of the set — the one that is on — and Tab again leaves the set; Right Arrow, End, Left Arrow and Home move focus in the order given and stop at the ends; in a right-to-left layout Left Arrow moves to the next chip; Shift+Tab after leaving comes back to the chip that last had focus.

behavior.text: WHILE selection is single or multiple, WHEN a member leaves while focus is on it THE tag group SHALL move focus as TGR-9 says, and the chip that then has focus SHALL be the set's stop; WHEN the chip that was the set's stop leaves, is disabled or no longer takes focus while focus is elsewhere THE tag group SHALL make a stop as TGR-20 says of a group whose last-focused chip is gone, so that the set keeps exactly one stop while it holds a chip that takes focus. WHEN selection becomes none THE tag group SHALL give each chip its own stop again.
behavior.verify: Unit: of five input chips under selection multiple, Delete on the focused third puts focus on the former fourth, which is then the only chip in the Tab order.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute on the host, by the attribute or by the ARIA property that reflects it, THE tag group SHALL move it to the data-aria- attribute of the same name, so that the host is no second node with its name, description or state, and SHALL expose it on its list — an id reference by the elements it names in the host's tree or a tree around it, a description after its own. WHILE label is not empty it is the list's name, over a name given so; WHILE label is empty, a name given so is the list's name. WHEN the product removes the aria- attribute or its data-aria- twin, or sets the ARIA property that reflects it (ariaLabel, ariaDescribedByElements…) to null, THE tag group SHALL take it off that element.

keyboard.action: While selection is none: moves focus to each chip of the set in turn, in the order given; an input chip is one stop, its remove action is not in the Tab order. While selection is single or multiple: the set is one stop — the chip that last had focus, else the first chip that is on, else the first chip (TGR-20). A set of tags has no stop.

keyboard.keys: Left Arrow / Right Arrow, Home / End
keyboard.action: While selection is single or multiple: move focus to the chip drawn before or after (the way the arrow points, in a right-to-left layout too), or to the first or the last, without switching anything; focus does not wrap. Up and Down Arrow do nothing. While selection is none the group handles no key.

The focused chip's own keys, as the Chip says: Space switches a filter chip — and, while selection is single or multiple, changes the group's selection (TGR-19); Backspace or Delete removes an input chip. After a removal, focus is on the chip that followed, or on the one before where none follows (TGR-9).

accessibility.labeling: label names the list ("Tags", "Filters"); it is not drawn. Each member is one list item and keeps its own name inside it: a tag its text, a chip its label, an input chip's remove action its removeLabel. A filter chip's state is its own pressed state, also while the group holds the selection: the chip then shows the group's selection. An empty group exposes nothing.
notes: Not interactive by itself: the tag group never takes focus itself, and while selection is none it handles no key (TGR-6), so it has no target of its own to size and minimumTarget holds through its chips, each of which extends its own hit area (CHP-5). What the group owes them is room: gap and row-gap decide how much of each extended hit area a chip keeps beside and between its neighbours (TGR-5).

Why a list, for tags and for chips alike: a list tells a person how many members there are and where they are among them, which is what a set of like things needs — four tags on an article, the third of nine filters. It holds static text, links and buttons equally, so one component needs no setting for its semantics.

Why not a group: a group says that controls belong together and nothing more. It is what a button group is, whose two to four members are different actions; a tag group's members are of one kind and any number.

Why not a list box, also while the group holds a selection: a list box is one control whose options hold the selection (aria-selected), and an option cannot hold a button — an input chip's remove action, or the chip's own button — inside it. React Aria's TagGroup exposes a selectable set as a grid, rows that carry aria-selected and the remove button in a cell; Tanrei's chip is a button whose pressed state already says whether it is on, which is how M3's filter chips and Carbon's selectable tags say it, so a selection keeps the list and each chip its pressed state. One choice among several that is not a filter is a radio group, tabs or a segmented button; a choice from a list is a select.

Why one stop with arrow keys only with a selection: while selection is none each chip is its own Tab stop, as every Button of a button group is (CHP-23), and a set of links or of entered items is crossed by Tab. A set that holds a selection is one control to the person who uses it, as a segmented button's segments and Material's chip set are: one stop, the arrow keys inside it (TGR-20), focus not wrapping, as in the chip field (CHF-13). The list stays, so a screen reader still says how many chips there are and where one is among them.

While selection is none the tag group does not make filter chips exclusive and holds no value: each filter chip is on or off by itself. With selection single the group puts one on at a time and a chip that is on can be switched off, leaving none, because each chip is a toggle; a choice that must always hold one value is a segmented button or a radio group. With multiple any number are on. The group names its chips by their value, as a segmented button names its segments, and its change carries value or values, as the segmented button's does (TGR-19).

After the last member is removed the group is gone and cannot hold focus. The product moves focus to what the set belonged to (the field that adds items, the button that opens the filters); otherwise the platform drops it. The docs page says so with an example.

Removing and selecting together: an input chip has no selected state (CHP-11), so in a set that holds a selection the entered items are reached by the arrow keys and removed by Backspace or Delete as before, and the filter chips are switched; the chip that receives focus after a removal becomes the set's stop (TGR-21). A filter chip that the product takes away leaves value and values as they were (TGR-17): the product, which took it away, changes them where it wants the filter gone.
A removal is not announced by the group. Where it must be (a filter removed far from the list it changes), the product reports it in a live region or with a snackbar.
A status among a set of tags never rests on color alone: each tag says it in words (TAG-11).

A small chip is for dense places where a set stands on one line. On wrapped lines small chips are 24 high and 16 apart under the default system, so their touch targets meet between the lines at 40; a set of small chips that wraps on a touch screen wants medium chips.
Text size: at 200% members grow and the set wraps onto more lines; nothing is cut by the group (TGR-12).

Compose and React Native have no list role for an arbitrary layout: the group is a traversal group whose content description is label and whose collection information gives the count (Compose), or a labelled container (React Native), and each member keeps its own role.

props.label: A note on why the documentation of a design system should be built from the components it documents, and what that taught us

web.name: tanrei-tag-group

chip.name: tanrei-chip
chip.notes: A `tanrei-chip` child, as anywhere; `remove-label` is its attribute. The page removes the element on `remove`; the group sees it leave and moves focus (TGR-9).

web.notes: `<tanrei-tag-group label="Filters" spacing="chips">` holds `tanrei-tag` and `tanrei-chip` children. The members stay in the product's light DOM, in the default slot: they keep their attributes, events, styles and place in the document, and the group moves none of them. The shadow root holds one element with `role="list"` and `aria-label`, a flex container that wraps (`flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; column-gap; row-gap` from the tokens of `spacing`), around the slot; the host has no role, and the group gives each slotted member `role="listitem"` where it has no role of its own and takes it back when the member leaves (`slotchange`), as the carousel exposes its items. A `tanrei-chip` host carries no role itself — its button or link is in its shadow root — so the item holds that control. While the slot is empty the host is `display: none` and the list is not rendered (TGR-8). Removal: a `MutationObserver` and `slotchange` find a member that left while `:focus-within` held on it, and the group calls `focus()` on the next chip (TGR-9). The debug report of TGR-4 looks for a `tanrei-chip` among the slotted elements. Before the element is defined its children are already shown, as the inline elements they are, in source order and separated by the white space between them: a set of tags is readable and a set of chips is operable once the chips themselves are defined; a page that wants the final layout from the first paint adds `tanrei-tag-group:not(:defined) { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: … }` with the token's custom properties. The host is `display: block`. Selection (TGR-17 to TGR-21): `selection` and `value` are attributes and properties; `values` is a property (an array), and the `values` attribute is also read, as JSON or as space-separated words, because the fixture harness writes attributes. A chip's `value` is the `tanrei-chip`'s own `value`. While selection is single or multiple the group writes each filter chip's `selected`, stops the chip's `change` at the host and dispatches its own `change` (`detail.value` or `detail.values`), and gives every chip but the set's stop `tabindex="-1"` (a host that delegates focus with a negative tabindex is out of the Tab order, with everything in its shadow root), taking back only the tabindex it gave; it handles the arrow keys, Home and End from a `keydown` listener on the host.

swiftui.name: TanreiTagGroup
swiftui.notes: `TanreiTagGroup(_ label: String = "", spacing: .chips) { TanreiChip(…) … }`: a custom `Layout` that flows its subviews into lines by TGR-1 and TGR-2 and follows `layoutDirection`. The container is `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` with the label; SwiftUI has no list trait for an arbitrary layout, so VoiceOver reads the label and then each member (TGR-7's fallback). Focus after a removal uses `@AccessibilityFocusState` and `@FocusState` keyed by the members' identities, which the caller gives with `.id(_:)` as in a `ForEach`. Selection: `TanreiTagGroup(selection: $value)` with a `Binding<String?>` (single) or a `Binding<Set<String>>` (multiple), each chip given its value as `TanreiChip(value:)`; the arrow keys come from `focusable()` and `onMoveCommand`.

compose.name: TanreiTagGroup

tag.name: TanreiTag
tag.notes: A `TanreiTag` call in the group's content, as anywhere.

chip.name: TanreiChip
chip.notes: A `TanreiChip` call in the group's content, as anywhere; `enabled` is disabled's inverse.

compose.notes: `TanreiTagGroup(spacing = TanreiTagGroupSpacing.Chips, contentDescription = "Filters") { … }`, built on `FlowRow` with the tokens' horizontal and vertical arrangements. Semantics: a traversal group with `contentDescription` and `collectionInfo` (one row, as many columns as members), each member given `collectionItemInfo`; TalkBack then reads the count. Focus after a removal: the group keeps a `FocusRequester` per member key and requests the next one when a focused member leaves the composition.

flutter.name: TanreiTagGroup

chip.name: TanreiChip
chip.notes: A `TanreiChip` in `children`, as anywhere. Give each a `Key`, so that the group can tell which one left.

flutter.notes: `TanreiTagGroup(spacing: TanreiTagGroupSpacing.chips, semanticLabel: 'Filters', children: […])`, built on `Wrap` with `spacing`, `runSpacing` and `crossAxisAlignment: WrapCrossAlignment.center`; `Wrap` follows `Directionality`. `Semantics(container: true, label:)` around it; Flutter has no list role for a `Wrap`, so the members are read in order after the label. Focus after a removal: the group compares its children's keys between builds and requests focus on the next chip's `FocusNode`.

react-native.name: TagGroup

chip.name: Chip
chip.notes: A `Chip` child, as anywhere. Give each a `key`, so that the group can tell which one left.

react-native.notes: `<TagGroup spacing="chips" accessibilityLabel="Filters">{…}</TagGroup>`: a `View` with `flexDirection: 'row'`, `flexWrap: 'wrap'`, `alignItems: 'center'`, `columnGap` and `rowGap` from the tokens, `accessibilityRole="list"` (announced on Android; a labelled container on iOS). It reads its children's keys to find the chip that follows a removed one and focuses it through its ref. Follows the app's direction where an ancestor's is not known.
